questions.question: Is L = {w ∈ {a,b}* : number of a's in w is even} regular?
questions.solutionApproach: Yes — a DFA with 2 states (tracking parity of a-count) accepts this. Bounded/modular counting is always regular.

questions.question: Is L = {a^n b^n c^n : n ≥ 0} regular?
questions.solutionApproach: No — requires matching THREE unbounded counts simultaneously, needs unbounded memory. Not regular (in fact, not even context-free).
questions.answer: No, not regular (requires unbounded matching of three counts).

questions.question: L is regular. Is the language {w : w is a prefix of some string in L} necessarily regular?
questions.solutionApproach: Yes — the 'prefix-closure' of a regular language is regular. Construct the automaton by marking as accepting ANY state from which an accepting state is reachable (not just the original accepting states).
questions.answer: Yes, always regular — prefix-closure preserves regularity.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of DFA states needed for L = {w ∈ {0,1}* : w ends in '01'}?
questions.solutionApproach: Myhill-Nerode: distinguishable states needed to track 'last 2 characters seen so far' relevant to matching '01' suffix — states: start/no-progress, seen-0(potential match start), seen-01(accept), and need to handle seen-1-after-0 vs other. Standard construction gives 3 states: q0(default), q1(just saw 0), q2(saw 01, accepting) — verify q2 on '0' goes to q1, on '1' goes to q0.
